en.title: Maximum Upgrades After Selling Some Servers
en.description:
Networks are independent. Each starts with n servers and funds money; selling a server yields sell, and upgrading a server costs upgrade. A sold server can no longer be upgraded. Find the maximum number of servers that can be upgraded in each network.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains the number of networks q, followed by q lines of num_servers money sell upgrade. 1≤q≤100000, and all four values are in 1..10000.
en.output: First output the number of networks, then output the maximum number of upgrades for each network.
en.explanation:
The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 2
3 2; 1
0; 1
10. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: If x servers are kept and upgraded, at most n−x can be sold. Therefore x≤n and x(upgrade+sell)≤money+n×sell; just round down.
